goal: Explain how a cross-device Agent workspace shares long-term context while keeping engineering and raw-file sources of truth separate.
narrative: Agents enter through one access layer, retrieve high-value context, act through tools, and keep versioned or raw artifacts in their authoritative stores.
scope: Logical responsibilities from Agent entry through memory, integrations, and durable artifact stores; deployment topology and concrete auth protocols are outside scope.
must_show: Multiple device and Agent entry points
GitHub as engineering source of truth
File storage as raw-content source of truth
Request to retrieval to execution to write-back loop
emphasize: Memory is the context center, not a replacement for all storage
GitHub and file storage have distinct authoritative responsibilities
Only high-value conclusions return to memory
relationships: Raw assets persist to file stores
uncertainties: The exact authentication protocol is unspecified
The exact synchronization mechanism between memory and artifact stores is unspecified
assumptions: Access control is shown as a gateway responsibility without naming a protocol
The architecture is logical rather than a deployment topology
content_risks: Do not imply memory stores every raw file or code artifact
Do not imply GitHub provides semantic memory
Do not invent trust zones or runtime regions
Do not give every integration the same weight as the memory/source-of-truth distinction
quality_questions: Can a viewer identify the role of memory versus GitHub and file storage within five seconds?
Is the long-term context layer visually central without implying it owns every artifact?
Is the main request to context to execution to write-back path obvious?
Are logical responsibilities separated from unspecified implementation details?
Are external tools visibly integrations rather than authoritative memory stores?

review_answers.question: Can a viewer identify the role of memory versus GitHub and file storage within five seconds?
review_answers.evidence: Memory has a dedicated central green band; GitHub and files are separately labelled inside the blue source-of-truth band.

review_answers.question: Is the long-term context layer visually central without implying it owns every artifact?
review_answers.evidence: The memory grid is the largest capability block, while artifact responsibilities are explicitly separated below.

review_answers.question: Is the main request to context to execution to write-back path obvious?
review_answers.evidence: Semantic vertical links and the numbered six-step data-flow strip expose the complete loop.

review_answers.question: Are logical responsibilities separated from unspecified implementation details?
review_answers.evidence: Labels describe responsibilities and omit concrete protocols, regions, and deployment units.

review_answers.question: Are external tools visibly integrations rather than authoritative memory stores?
review_answers.evidence: Tools occupy their own orange integration band and are not nested inside memory or source-of-truth blocks.
